subject: Competitive intel: pricing & model moves — QBR prep
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive intel: pricing & model moves — QBR prep

Team,

High-level roundup ahead of next week’s QBR — extracted from sales intel, partner notes, and public announcements. This is a leadership-level briefing; please read and flag anything that should be surfaced to the board or our enterprise customers.

Key items:
- CloudCo announced a transient price cut (up to 30% on high-throughput endpoints) for 3 months, effective Feb 15. Internal note: likely a demand play for enterprise renewals.
- Orpheus AI released Atlas-2 (open checkpoint) claiming 2x throughput for medium-length context and native 8-bit quantization optimizations. Early bench results show latency gains but mixed quality on long-form summarization.
- A smaller startup (Embeddly) launched a managed embeddings service with usage-based compression and a free tier. Could impact Optimize adoption for small customers.

Implications for our QBR narrative / OKRs:
1) Pricing: Sales will ask for guidance. Recommend positioning: emphasize total cost of ownership (latency SLAs, reliability, model rollouts, and predictable reserved capacity) rather than per-token list price. Consider a short-term defensive credit program for at-risk renewals (ops ask: what’s the cost of a 3-month targeted credit?).
2) Product: Highlight dedicated autoscaling and cache guarantees as differentiation vs. Atlas-2 throughput claims. Engineering: need a 1-slide perf comparison (latency @ 512/1024 tokens) by Monday.
3) GTM: Add a talking point on embeddings quality + storage savings vs. Embeddly. Growth/sales to get a one-pager.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Markus: draft pricing stance + proposed 3-month credit bucket and approval path (deadline: Mon EOD).
- Evelyn: collect top-5 enterprise questions we should proactively address in QBRs (deadline: Mon noon).
- Vivek: short perf slides or pointers to bench runs, with recommended callouts (deadline: Mon EOD).

Attachments: I’m attaching a short competitor brief and an early QBR deck draft. Please don’t share externally yet.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: competitor-brief-20260212.pdf (pdf, 3 pages), QBR-deck-draft-v1.pptx (pptx, 12 slides)

> - Orpheus AI released Atlas-2 (open checkpoint) claiming 2x throughput for medium-length context and native 8-bit quantization optimizations.
> - A smaller startup (Embeddly) launched a managed embeddings service with usage-based compression and a free tier.

Laura — thanks for the concise summary. A few quick points from pricing/sales ops perspective:
- We should avoid reacting on list price. Proposal: offer two defensive levers for renewals — (A) one-time invoice credit tied to usage velocity, or (B) a 3-month reserved window with a capped overage rate. Both require finance sign-off but we can model the $ impact quickly.
- Request: legal & finance need a templated email/contract addendum for quick approvals. Can Rachel (billing) stand up a draft? (cc’ing offline).

I’ll take point on a short memo with example scenarios (low/med/high usage) and a suggested credit runway. Will circulate by Mon EOD.

-Markus
Head of Sales Strategy
Redwood Inference

Quick customer color from CS:
- Three mid-market customers flagged CloudCo’s announcement during renewal conversations this week; main objection is price, but they repeatedly call out our rollout guarantees and lower error rates as differentiators.
- One large account (Acme Corp — Sarah Lee) asked for a direct comparison to Atlas-2 performance on summarization and hallucination rate. They’re a top QBR customer — recommend we prepare an appendix slide showing quality benchmarks and regeneration costs.

I’ll consolidate the top customer questions and sample language for the QBR slide. Will include suggested mitigation lines for cheaper-list competitors (emphasize predictability, auditability, and private deployments). Due: Mon 12pm.

—Evelyn
Director, Customer Success

- Deck: I updated the QBR draft (v1) with a competitive slide and the recommended talking points. Attached for review.

Deadline recap: Mon 12pm (Evelyn), Mon EOD (Markus & Vivek). Please add edits directly to the deck in Drive. If you see anything we should escalate to the board or legal, flag me.

Laura
